intention: Both Supercharger tables are keyed on tesla_id, account_id is gone, the mirror runs one pass per vehicle, and VerifySession cannot be called without a vehicleref.Ref.
request: MAG-67 — 4. Re-key the Supercharger pair on tesla_id; reshape the mirror. Step 4 of MAG-63.

decisions.what: tesla_id becomes NOT NULL on both Supercharger tables; account_id is dropped from both.
decisions.why: Nothing but account_id ties a supercharger_history row to an account. After the drop an orphan row (tesla_id IS NULL) is unreachable by any query, so keeping the column nullable saves nothing.

decisions.what: The migration deletes rows where tesla_id IS NULL before SET NOT NULL.
decisions.why: Owner confirmed after checking: both tables hold 0 such rows today, so the DELETE is a guard, not a data loss. The down-migration cannot restore a deleted row.

decisions.what: Run as roadmap RM57 with three tiers (telemetry, charging, gateway) instead of one standalone change.
decisions.why: Two modules each own a migration and the mirror between them is reshaped. Three smaller proposals are easier to review than one large one.

decisions.what: Tier 3 is owned by gateway; the internal/app and internal/analytics call-site updates inside it are leader-owned integration work.
decisions.why: A worker is sandboxed to one module. Port signature changes ripple into app and analytics, which is cross-module integration the leader owns by contract.

decisions.what: collectChargingHistory skips a session whose VIN is not a registered vehicle, and counts the skip in CycleReport.
decisions.why: RD1 makes tesla_id NOT NULL, so the row cannot be written. A silent skip would hide it; counting it mirrors the existing ChargingFetchFailures shape.

decisions.what: Index plan approved: vehicle_time and account_updated re-keyed on tesla_id, account_time dropped with no replacement.
decisions.why: account_time's only reader was SuperchargerHistoryByAccount, which this change removes. The new (tesla_id, updated_at) index also removes a sort the mirror read pays today.

decisions.what: processor.go fans out over each account's vehicles now, keeping the account-keyed watermark. Tier 3 still does the per-vehicle rewrite.
decisions.why: SuperchargerHistoryByAccountUpdatedSince cannot survive the column drop, and it has a production caller. The fan-out uses a port that already exists, so tier 3 undoes nothing.

decisions.what: SuperchargerHistoryByAccount and SuperchargerHistoryByAccountUpdatedSince are removed, not re-keyed.
decisions.why: Both filter on account_id alone. Dropping the parameter would leave a whole-table scan. The roadmap's 'drop accountID' line only fits the three per-vehicle methods.

decisions.what: Tier 2's artifact worker runs on Opus, not the Sonnet default.
decisions.why: Two migrations, a unique-constraint swap and an index plan judged against live queries. Tier 1's equivalent dispatch also used Opus.

decisions.what: Sessions DDL and index plan approved: UNIQUE (session_id), tesla_id NOT NULL, account_id dropped, one index (tesla_id, charge_stop_date_time).
decisions.why: All three reads order by charge_stop_date_time. A btree walks backwards at the same cost, so the newest-first read needs no second index. No updated_at index.

decisions.what: The migration deletes every charging.mirror_watermarks cursor instead of mapping it onto each vehicle.
decisions.why: The table's own comment says an absent cursor means re-read the whole history once. The mirror is an idempotent upsert, so the cost is one longer nightly run.

decisions.what: VerifySession is re-keyed on tesla_id, not stripped of its scope.
decisions.why: Its account_id predicate is the only tenant check on the Supercharger write path; the handler does none. The gateway supplies the vehicle from resolveSelectedVehicle, which is account-scoped.

decisions.what: The per-vehicle mirror rewrite in internal/app/processor.go moves from tier 3 into tier 2 (task T8).
decisions.why: Re-keying the watermark leaves the account-grouped loop with no cursor to read. Splitting them would stop the nightly mirror between the two tiers.

decisions.what: VerifySession is retyped to take a vehicleref.Ref. The three ListSessionsByVehicle* read ports keep int64.
decisions.why: internal/analytics calls the read ports and vehicleref-guard forbids building a Ref outside the gateway's authorizeVehicle. Only the gateway-only write port can be retyped without holing the guard.

decisions.what: The two Supercharger read sites keep resolveSelectedVehicle; a comment and design.md record that its RegisteredVehicles filter is the ownership proof.
decisions.why: Adding authorizeVehicle there runs a second account query per render and discards the Ref, since the read ports keep int64. No new guarantee for a real cost.

decisions.what: SuperchargerRowUpdate takes the vehicle id from currentVehicle(c), not resolveSelectedVehicle, then proves it with authorizeVehicle.
decisions.why: One account query instead of two. A save always follows a render that set the cookie, so no selection means a stale or hand-crafted POST, where 404 is the right answer.

decisions.what: The old tier 3 splits into tier 3 (charging, retype VerifySession) and tier 4 (gateway, call authorizeVehicle).
decisions.why: RD14 pulls a port definition into internal/charging. A worker is sandboxed to one module and config.yaml forbids one change spanning two.

decisions.what: make vehicleref-guard now exempts _test.go files. The leader made the Makefile and internal/vehicleref/AGENTS.md edits, not the worker.
decisions.why: MAG-66's design always described that exemption; the target was built without it. Both files sit outside internal/charging, so a sandboxed worker cannot touch them.

decisions.what: Tier 4 is built before tier 3 is reviewed and archived, reversing the roadmap's own depends_on order.
decisions.why: make test cannot build while the gateway call site is broken, so the owner had no way to run the suite. Tier 4 restores the build; both tiers are then reviewed together.

decisions.what: One worker writes tier 4's artifacts and implements them in the same dispatch.
decisions.why: No database object changes, so no design gate fires, and RD15 and RD16 already settled every design choice. A separate artifact round would decide nothing.

budget.note: Sum of tier 1's wave and review deltas across three sessions: waves 1-3 (+11,+18,+17), review round 1 + its fixes (+13), plus the wave-4 fix and archive. Spans two 5-hour buckets, so the pct is additive within buckets only.

tiers.notes: Archived to openspec/changes/archive/charging/2026-09-14-RM57-charging-rekey-supercharger-sessions-on-tesla-id. Reviewer approved in round 2. Owner verified the suite twice - once after wave 3, once after the round-1 fixes. RD13 moved the processor.go rewrite here from tier 3.
